I checked the vfinal fix pass at dc3ba85 for feel and world. Both claims hold. The hurt vignette's depth is now bounded. The rear Bruiser smash at hurt f2186-2188 tops out at 0.316 of the screen height, against 0.599 at 3e7084e. The three rear pipe hits (f3682/3714/3748) peak at 0.227, 0.236 and 0.229, against 0.36, 0.43 and 0.47 before. In the new rear run the smashes give 0.20, 0.30 and 0.30 and the pipes 0.24, 0.21 and 0.25, so the depth does not climb from hit to hit. The front smash is pixel-identical (0.311). A probe of 400 random hits never pushed the depth past 0.320 or any stored edge past 0.973. Putting the old ratchet back makes 6 of the 49 feel tests fail; the head passes 49/49.

The world changes match the 82bab12 look bar wherever trim now wins: the warehouse jamb (f201), the a2 lintel (f97), the skyline_up pilaster edge and door reveal (f305), and the catwalk rail top (f763). The skyline reveal is now a steady dark face; 82bab12 showed dark there in 29 of 39 held frames. Held-pose flicker matches 3e7084e at all 20 tour poses, and ground_flicker on the drift recording gives identical numbers. The rooms are pixel-identical. No Dressing piece went missing or doubled, and no clipped face's shading changed.

There is one new cosmetic low. The bottom-teeth floor turns a light rear hit's spikes into a regular row of seven equal teeth, where every other edge, and 3e7084e's bottom edge, draws jagged teeth of varied length.

findings.title: The bottom-stroke floor makes a light rear hit's spikes a regular row of seven equal teeth
findings.detail: VF2-FEEL replaced the 1.4x bottom stroke gain with a per-tooth floor: length = maxf(natural, hurt_overlay_bottom_stroke_floor * size.y). For a Punk's 6-damage hit from behind (the most common rear blow in a crowd), every tooth's natural length (0.18 x (0.55..1.25) x 0.95 = 0.09-0.21 of the height) falls under the 0.20 floor. So all seven teeth are drawn exactly 0.20 tall: a flat picket instead of the jagged comic spikes that every other edge draws, and that the bottom drew at 3e7084e (0.12-0.24, varied). The front jab's top teeth on the same frame stay varied. The hit still reads as plainly (the band metric is unchanged), so this is cosmetic. Heavy rear hits keep their variation, because their natural lengths mostly exceed the floor.
findings.evidence: Probe GUT test on dc3ba85 (200 seeded hits each): rear 6 dmg, the tallest tooth at p10/p50/p90 is 0.200/0.200/0.208 and all teeth sit at the floor in 85% of hits; front 6 dmg top teeth at p10/p50/p90 0.183/0.204/0.213, varied. Recording: captures/m6-vf2-final/hurt/bot.avi f619 against captures/m6-verify-final/hurt/bot.avi f619 (rear jab bottom strip), with the front jab f100 top strip below (/Users/arachne/repos/beat-em-up-PoC/.worktrees/m6-review-vf2check-feelworld/captures/review/rear_jab_comb.png). The same flat row shows at f7649 (look-down rear jab) and f2846 (rear shove). Code: game/ui/hurt_overlay.gd _stroke_shapes(), the maxf(..., floor_px) on the length.
findings.repro: Play the hurt act's 'punk jab behind' (or let any Punk jab you from behind) and look at the bottom edge: seven identical triangles. Unit test: HurtOverlay at 1600x900, on_player_hit with damage 6 and direction (0,0,-1), then stroke_lengths_px(Edge.BOTTOM) returns seven equal values of 180 px.
findings.suggested_fix: In game/ui/hurt_overlay.gd _stroke_shapes(), keep the comb's variation while lifting it. Scale the whole bottom comb by k = maxf(1.0, floor_px / tallest_natural_length), so the tallest tooth reaches the floor and the others keep their proportions. Or floor each tooth at floor_px times its own random share (len_min + r * len_range) / (len_min + len_range), so the shortest stays near the floor and the rest spread above it. No new tunable is needed. Re-pin the 'a light jab's bottom teeth are at least the floor' test to 'the tallest bottom tooth is at least the floor'.

findings.title: BOARD_EDGE cut also removes a plinth's top ledge when the rectangle starts exactly at the plinth top
findings.detail: MeshClip._outside_edge keeps an edge face only if its coordinate lies outside the rectangle's span plus or minus tolerance. A ledge at v equal to rect.position.y (a partner whose face starts exactly where the plinth ends and continues upward) is therefore cut across the rectangle's u span. The plinth front below it (v below the rectangle) is kept, so the plinth is left with an open top, which back-face culling shows as a hole. The same logic is correct when the rectangle ends at the plinth top. No scene in the level triggers it: a probe over all 198 cut edge triangles found none at an interior boundary. It is a latent edge case in the new rule. The orphan scan cannot see it, because it only counts triangles left inside a clipped rectangle.
findings.evidence: game/level/kit/mesh_clip.gd _outside_edge, the `at < rect.position.x - tolerance or at > rect.end.x + tolerance` test. Probe on KitMesh.build(&"wall", Vector3(6,4,0.6)), whose ledge is at y = -1.4: clip_box with Rect2(-3, -1.4, 6, 3.4) on the +z face takes the ledge from 2 triangles to 0 while the board's front stays.
findings.repro: In a GUT test, mesh = KitMesh.build(&"wall", Vector3(6,4,0.6)); cut = MeshClip.clip_box(mesh, Vector3(6,4,0.6), {MeshClip.key(2,1): [Rect2(-3.0, -1.4, 6.0, 3.4)] as Array[Rect2]}, 0.06, 0.004); count triangles with a y normal near y = -1.4 and z above 0.304: 2 before, 0 after, with the board's front face still present.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep an edge face whose coordinate lies on the rectangle's lower bound when the board's front face below it is kept. Cut only edge faces strictly inside the span, plus those on the upper bound or on a side the rectangle covers on both sides. Add a unit test for a rectangle that starts at the plinth top.

findings.title: tools/apply_yields.py breaks the section scenes when run on an empty or stripped output (it deletes the inset_blk ext_resource and cannot re-add it)
findings.detail: apply_yields.py removes the `inset_blk` ext_resource line when no block uses it, and it only swaps script references, it never adds the declaration back. Running it once with a solver output that has no YIELD lines, to strip the scenes the way the docstring invites, deletes that ext_resource. A second run with the real output then writes 97 `ExtResource("inset_blk")` references without a declaration, and street, roofs and boss_roof all fail to parse. Stripping the yields_to lines by hand (the documented step) and re-running the solver and the apply tool works, with zero diff against the committed scenes. This is a trap in a tool, not in the shipped build.
findings.evidence: I ran `python3 tools/apply_yields.py empty.txt`, then the solver, then `apply_yields.py solve.txt`. Godot then fails with `Parse Error ... street.tscn:58`, `roofs.tscn:85` and `boss_roof.tscn:133`, and street.tscn holds 17 `ExtResource("inset_blk")` references and 0 `id="inset_blk"` declarations. The tool's code is the `used = ...` / `re.sub` ext_resource removal near the end of main().
findings.repro: git checkout the scenes; python3 tools/apply_yields.py <empty file>; run tools/solve_insets.tscn; python3 tools/apply_yields.py <its output>; godot --headless --import --quit and load the level.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-insert the ext_resource declaration when a block needs it (or never delete it), and say in the docstring that the strip step is `sed '/^yields_to = /d'`, not running the tool on empty input.

findings.title: Roll-out closure test still accepts a const named only inside a string or assigned to an unused variable
findings.detail: The two repro files of vfinal-code-02 now fail. The tightened `_roll_out_file_problem` still lets a character through if a test body merely mentions the const's name as a whole word, including inside a string literal (`assert_true(true, "P")`) or in `var x := P`. A helper that only another helper calls (a two-level chain) is not followed, so the check is stricter than needed there. The character is still kept out of the shared guards only by a test that mentions its config, not one that must read it.
findings.evidence: tests/test_m6_feedback_detail.gd `_names_any` (a regex word match on the raw body, strings not stripped). I ran `_roll_out_file_problem` on a file with `const P := ".../characters/thug/pipeline.json"` and `func test_a(): assert_true(true, "P")`; it returned an empty string (pass). `func test_t(): var x := _b()` where `_b` only calls `_a`, which reads P, returned a failure (a false negative).
findings.repro:
Load the test script, instantiate it, and call _roll_out_file_problem("extends GutTest
const P := "res://assets/source/characters/thug/pipeline.json"
func test_a() -> void:
	assert_true(true, "P")
", "thug").
findings.suggested_fix: Blank string literals before the identifier match, and follow helpers transitively. Optionally require a FileAccess, load or JSON call with the const.
